title: Address the AMP learner review and retain the offline discriminator evidence
summary: The program lead's review of the AMP learner found that every AMP checkpoint would fail evaluation: the learner configuration held a tuple that its JSON record stores as a list. The configuration is now JSON-shaped, and the evaluate checks are functions with tests for matching, mismatched and pre-learner records. The discriminator initializes on a forked generator, so parity with stock PPO holds from one seed. A partial load restores only what the caller names. The learner tests use bank-scale states. The reward pull request's discriminator and its test are restored unchanged; the learner owns its standardized-input gradient penalty. A retained offline report replaces the unbound numbers in update 20260925T204923_amp_learner: on the admitted bank the raw-input penalty starts at 3886 and leaves every style reward near 0.76, while the standardized penalty scores held-out bank transitions 0.94 and the recorded policy trace 0.12. The earlier statement that the task reward must penalize standing is withdrawn: a discriminator that never saw standing transitions scores them 0.99, and one trained with them as negatives scores them 0.11. Neither measures the online learner.
next: Ask the reward pull request's author whether amp_discriminator should adopt the standardized-input penalty. Measure a standing policy against the online discriminator in the first native pilot before deciding how the task reward treats standing.
reason: CPU corrections, tests and an offline diagnostic; no native run, checkpoint, roadmap marker or acceptance gate changes.
